subject.title: [Feature]: Slim the Skill Workshop system-prompt section; move mechanics into the tool schema

question: Should OpenClaw accept the slimmer Skill Workshop prompt/schema wording as sufficient to preserve the governed proposal-routing contract?
rationale: The requested cleanup reduces recurring prompt bytes and improves tone, but it changes model-facing instructions around a safety-sensitive skill-write boundary; tests can check strings, but maintainers must choose the acceptable wording redundancy.

options.title: Approve after proof
options.body: Accept the prompt/schema split once the linked PR includes real prompt/schema output or a redacted transcript showing the slimmed text and preserved routing rule.

options.title: Tighten wording first
options.body: Ask the PR to keep one additional lifecycle sentence if maintainers want more explicit apply/reject/quarantine guardrails in the always-paid prompt.

options.title: Keep verbose guardrails
options.body: Leave the current repeated prompt text in place if maintainers prefer redundant model-facing safety language over prompt-byte savings and softer tone.

recommendation.title: Approve after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the prompt/schema split once the linked PR includes real prompt/schema output or a redacted transcript showing the slimmed text and preserved routing rule.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter owns the protected request and authored the linked candidate implementation, making him the strongest routing candidate for the wording tradeoff.
